skill.name: brainstorming
skill.description: Guides early product and engineering ideas through structured questions, alternative exploration, incremental validation, and planning handoff.
skill.summary: Refines rough ideas into validated designs before implementation begins.
skill.author: DYAI2025

security_audit.summary: The markdown file contains structured brainstorming instructions and examples, not executable shell or Ruby code. The command-related static findings are false positives caused by markdown code fences, while the bundled ZIP remains unscanned and should be manually reviewed before publication.

remediation.issue: Bundled archive was not statically scanned.
remediation.suggestion: Extract and review SKILL.zip, then include only necessary plain-text skill files in the marketplace package.

Lines 61-67 contain a structured choice example about architecture options. The backticks are markdown formatting and no executable command is present.
The flagged text is the end of a markdown example followed by process guidance. It does not contain command execution behavior.
Lines 119-136 are a Graphviz DOT diagram in a fenced block. The diagram is static documentation and is not a shell command or execution instruction.
Line 66 only names a product architecture option, "Hybrid with background jobs." It does not request system discovery, enumeration, or reconnaissance.
The archive was not statically scanned, so its contents cannot be verified from the available analysis. This is a supply-chain review gap rather than evidence of malicious behavior.

content.value_statement: Rough ideas often turn into weak plans when teams skip discovery. This skill guides Claude, Codex, or Claude Code through focused questions, option comparison, and staged design validation.
actual_capabilities: Starts a brainstorming session with a clear announcement and structured process.
Asks one clarifying question at a time to gather goals, constraints, and success criteria.
Presents two or three solution approaches with trade-offs and complexity notes.
Validates design sections incrementally before moving toward implementation.
Directs handoff to worktree setup and planning skills when implementation is approved.
limitations: Does not implement code by itself.
Depends on user answers for accurate requirements and constraints.
References companion skills that may not exist in every environment.
Does not validate technical feasibility with tests or runtime checks.

use_cases.title: Shape a new product feature
use_cases.description: Turn an initial feature idea into goals, constraints, alternatives, and a validated design direction.

use_cases.title: Compare engineering architectures
use_cases.description: Explore multiple technical approaches before choosing the simplest design that meets the requirements.

use_cases.title: Prepare implementation planning
use_cases.description: Confirm the design in sections before moving into a detailed build plan or isolated worktree.

prompt_templates.title: Explore a rough idea
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the brainstorming skill to help me refine this idea: [describe the idea]. Ask one question at a time.

prompt_templates.title: Compare solution options
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the brainstorming skill to propose two or three approaches for [problem]. Include trade-offs and complexity for each option.

prompt_templates.title: Validate a design section by section
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the brainstorming skill to turn this direction into a design. Present it in short sections and pause for validation after each section: [context].

prompt_templates.title: Prepare for implementation handoff
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the brainstorming skill to check whether this design is ready for implementation planning: [design summary]. Identify missing decisions before planning.

output_examples.input: We need a better onboarding flow for new users.
output_examples.output: The assistant asks about target users, success criteria, and constraints. It then presents options such as guided setup, progressive onboarding, or checklist-based onboarding.

output_examples.input: Should we use events or direct API calls for this workflow?
output_examples.output: The assistant compares event-driven, synchronous, and hybrid designs. It explains trade-offs in reliability, complexity, latency, and debugging.

output_examples.input: Here is the chosen approach. Help me confirm the design before coding.
output_examples.output: The assistant presents architecture, components, data flow, error handling, and testing in short sections. It asks for validation after each section.

best_practices: Give the assistant clear context about users, goals, constraints, and success criteria.
Choose between proposed approaches before asking for detailed implementation planning.
Validate each design section and revise earlier assumptions when new constraints appear.
anti_patterns: Do not use it to skip requirements gathering and jump directly into code.
Do not ask for every possible approach when two or three options are enough.
Do not force a linear process when new information requires revisiting earlier phases.

faq.question: What does this skill do?
faq.answer: It helps turn a rough idea into a validated design through questions, alternatives, and staged review.

faq.question: Does it write implementation code?
faq.answer: No. It prepares the design and can hand off to planning after the user approves the direction.

faq.question: When should I use it?
faq.answer: Use it before implementation when goals, constraints, or architecture choices are still unclear.

faq.question: Can it help with technical architecture?
faq.answer: Yes. It asks clarifying questions and compares architecture options with trade-offs and complexity.

faq.question: Does it require other skills?
faq.answer: It references worktree setup and planning handoff skills for later phases, but the brainstorming flow can stand alone.

faq.question: Is it safe to use with sensitive project details?
faq.answer: The skill does not request secrets or external network activity. Users should still avoid sharing unnecessary confidential information.
